name: Coldseam Retired Spire Slummer's the Gray Zone Day Set
description: A bespoke Coldseam overcoat — once Φ4,000 worth of pressed wool-analog and chrome-thread piping — now patched at both elbows with the Gray Zone-grade duct tape and re-hemmed with mismatched thread. Worn over a stained Tier 3 dress shirt with the collar button missing and synth-leather trousers gone gray at the knees. The shoes are still Caelum IX pressure-forms, which is the tell.
functionality: Still structurally weatherproof despite damage; deep interior pockets retain their hidden lining compartments.
what_it_says: Someone who fell very far, very fast — and still hasn't let go of who they were.
worn_by: burned fixers with old money habits
manufacturer: Coldseam (original); the Gray Zone repairs by unknown hands
story_hooks: The coat's interior lining still has an encrypted Spire access chip sewn into the hem — its owner doesn't know it still works.
Someone in the Gray Zone recognizes the chrome-thread piping pattern and knows exactly which corponation this person used to run.
related_entities: Arcturus Defense Solutions ChemoShield BX-2 Dermal Toxin Barrier Implant
TESSERA CORPONATION Aegis CorpSec Hardened Security BCI

physical_description.visual_profile: A study in contradiction — haute couture gutted by time and poverty. Sharp tailored silhouette undermined by visible repairs and staining. The overcoat's structured shoulders still command presence despite the degradation. Worn by someone who remembers better circumstances.
physical_description.fit: Tailored through the chest and shoulders, slightly oversized through the body in a way that suggests weight loss or intentional slouching to hide the garment's true cut. Trousers hang straight but slack at the hips.
physical_description.primary_material: Pressed wool-analog overcoat (original Coldseam construction); Tier 3 synthetic cotton dress shirt; synth-leather trousers; Caelum IX pressure-form shoes
physical_description.texture: Overcoat: smooth, dense weave with subtle sheen from chrome-thread piping catching light. Duct tape patches: matte, rough, plasticky. Dress shirt: soft but worn thin at collar and cuffs. Trousers: leather-analog has developed a creased, papery texture at stress points. Shoes: molded pressure-form with subtle grip patterning, still maintaining slight iridescence.
physical_description.color_scheme: Overcoat: charcoal gray with silver chrome-thread accent piping along lapels and cuffs. Duct tape patches: industrial gray-silver. Dress shirt: off-white fading to yellow-brown at armpits and collar. Trousers: deep slate gray, faded to ash-gray at knees. Shoes: matte black with faint iridescent undertones.
physical_description.closures: Overcoat: magnetic snap buttons (original Coldseam hardware, still functional, showing tarnish). Dress shirt: worn plastic buttons, one missing at collar. Trousers: friction-fit waistband with deteriorated elastic. Shoes: pressure-form molded fit, no closures.
distinctive_features: Chrome-thread piping on overcoat lapels and cuffs still catching light despite overall wear
Asymmetrical duct tape patches at both elbows — right patch larger, applied more recently
Hand-repaired hem with mismatched thread (reddish polyester on charcoal wool)
Original Coldseam maker's mark still visible inside overcoat collar
Missing collar button on dress shirt, hole slightly frayed
Severe knee wear on trousers showing repeated kneeling or prolonged sitting
Caelum IX pressure-form shoes — the expensive holdout, still pristine relative to outfit
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional wear masquerading as Tier 1-2 heritage. The overcoat screams former wealth; everything else screams current poverty. Mixed signals that read as 'fallen' rather than 'never had.'
physical_description.cultural_context: Spire Slummer — someone who once occupied corporate housing (evident from Coldseam ownership) and has since dropped into the Gray Zone (mid-level ungoverned zones). Likely trades on former status or education. The refusal to discard Caelum IX shoes suggests stubborn pride or genuine attachment to last remaining asset. Military or medical background possible (pressure-forms indicate past augmentation access).
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn, patched, stained, fading. Not deliberately distressed — this is genuine weathering and repair from lack of resources. Maintained but not cared-for. The overcoat is dry-cleaned once annually if at all; the rest is hand-washed in cold water.
